editorial.headline: Professional Certification for Partners and Suppliers
editorial.standfirst: A foreign-open activity for second-party professional competency certification, with no Bali moratorium block indicated at its medium-high/high-risk level.
editorial.body:
This activity covers professional certification of human resources’ work or professional competence for the interests of a company’s partners and suppliers. In practical terms, it is framed as second-party professional certification: certification carried out in relation to the competence needs of an organisation’s own partner and supplier network.

The record is specific about that relationship. The activity is not presented simply as general education or training, but as certification connected to people working for partners and suppliers. Its focus is the assessment and certification of work or professional competence, serving the interests of those linked parties. No business-scale category is listed in the record, so it does not distinguish this activity by scale.

Nationally, the activity is marked open to foreign investment, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That is the national position supplied for this code, supported by Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. The record therefore presents no national foreign-ownership cap below full ownership for this activity.

Bali’s position is more address-sensitive than prohibitive. The activity is classified there as medium-high/high risk and is not blocked by Bali’s moratorium, which permanently blocks PMA registration for low- and medium-low-risk activities across the province. The record nevertheless directs verification for the specific address. For a prospective Bali registration, the clear reading is that the provincial moratorium is not the obstacle here, while the proposed location still needs to be checked.
